mainTopic: Whether witnesses who testified about the sale of a kidnapped person (עדי מכירה) are put to death when they are proven to be עדים זוממין, and whether חזקיה holds that a kidnapper who has not yet sold his victim gets מלקות.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation: in a בן סורר ומורה case, even חזקיה agrees that the later witnesses are executed if proven to be עדים זוממין. The reason is that the first witnesses can say 'we only came to get him lashes.' רב פפא applies the same logic to kidnapping and asks why the sale witnesses are not executed according to חזקיה. The גמרא proves that חזקיה holds a kidnapper who has not yet sold is lashed, so the question stands. רב פפא therefore explains the מחלוקת differently: everyone agrees the sale witnesses are executed, and the argument is only about the kidnapping witnesses. אביי then sums up which בן סורר ומורה cases are agreed and which one is disputed. רב אסי rules that sale witnesses are not executed because the accused can say 'I sold my slave.' The גמרא shows this fits even the רבנן, including a case where the two pairs of witnesses hinted to each other. Finally, a new משנה begins on the זקן ממרא: the three courts, and the rule that an elder is liable only for a practical ruling against the בית דין הגדול. The גמרא then opens a ברייתא on the פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The later witnesses did the whole thing
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the reasoning for why חזקיה agrees that the later witnesses in בן סורר ומורה are executed. The first witnesses can claim they only came to get him lashes, so the later witnesses are the ones who caused his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The first witnesses can say:] 'We came only to get him lashes.' So these other witnesses are the ones who did the entire thing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation of why, even according to חזקיה, the last set of witnesses in the case of a בן סורר ומורה are executed if they are proven to be עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בן סורר ומורה, the first testimony only leads to מלקות; only the later testimony leads to death. The first witnesses can honestly say their goal was just lashes. That puts all of the blame for the death sentence on the later witnesses, so they receive the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: the entire matter, the whole thing

phrases.english: We came to have him flogged,
phrases.notes: These words are what the first witnesses can say. The sentence began before this section, in the case of the בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: and these other witnesses
are doing the entire matter to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: להלקותו באנו, והני אחריני כוליה דבר קא עבדי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a sentence that began before this section: חזקיה's agreement about the later witnesses in בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the earlier witnesses can say they only meant to cause lashes, the later witnesses are fully responsible for the death sentence and are executed as עדים זוממין.

steps.title: Then the sale witnesses should also be executed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that the same logic should apply to kidnapping. The kidnapping witnesses can also say they only came for lashes, so the sale witnesses should be executed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: If so, the witnesses to the sale should also be executed, since the witnesses to the kidnapping can say, 'We came to get him lashes!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges חזקיה. If the 'we came for lashes' reasoning works for בן סורר ומורה, it should work for kidnapping as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kidnapper is only executed once he both kidnaps and sells. The kidnapping witnesses can claim they only came to get him lashes for the kidnapping alone. If so, the sale witnesses did 'the whole thing' and should be killed, but חזקיה earlier said they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: witnesses to the sale (of the kidnapped person)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, עֵידֵי מְכִירָה נָמֵי לִיקְטְלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: If so, let the witnesses to the sale also be executed,
since the witnesses to the kidnapping can say,
'We came to have him flogged!'

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה רב פפא: אי הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning of step 1 and applies it to kidnapping, where it seems to contradict חזקיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's ruling that the witnesses to the sale are not executed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'we came only for lashes' argument applies just as well to the kidnapping witnesses. That would make the sale witnesses fully responsible, just like the later witnesses in בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Maybe a kidnapper who has not sold gets no lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible defense of חזקיה: perhaps he holds that a kidnapper who has not sold is not lashed at all. If so, the kidnapping witnesses cannot say 'we came for lashes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that חזקיה holds that [a kidnapper without a sale] is not flogged...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way out for חזקיה. It is setting this up only so it can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If kidnapping without a sale carries no מלקות, then the kidnapping witnesses have no 'lashes' excuse. The comparison to בן סורר ומורה would then break down.

phrases.english: And if you would say
that חזקיה holds that he is not flogged,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the kidnapper who kidnapped but has not yet sold the person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי תימא דקסבר חזקיה דלא לקי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested distinction (one the גמרא will reject)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Kidnapping without a sale carries lashes, so the 'lashes' excuse works.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps חזקיה holds there are no lashes for kidnapping alone, so the excuse fails.

steps.title: A known dispute about lashes for kidnapping witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested defense by citing a known מחלוקת between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן. The question there is whether kidnapping witnesses who were proven false are lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was stated: kidnapping witnesses who were proven to be עדים זוממין, חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree. One says they are flogged, and one says they are not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the defense by quoting an earlier dispute. In that dispute, one of these two אמוראים holds that the kidnapping witnesses are flogged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין receive what they tried to do to the accused. So if the witnesses are flogged, that means the kidnapper himself would have been flogged. The next step will show which side is חזקיה's.

keyTerms.meaning: who were proven to be עדים זוממין

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated:
witnesses to the kidnapping of a person who were proven false,
phrases.notes: This means they were proven false before the sale witnesses testified.

phrases.english: Chizkiyya and Rabbi Yochanan disagree:
one says: they are flogged,
and one says: they are not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: והא איתמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the defense offered in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that חזקיה holds a kidnapper without a sale gets no lashes
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a known מחלוקת about lashes for false kidnapping witnesses, and (as the next step shows) חזקיה is the one who says they are flogged.

steps.title: Proof that חזקיה is the one who says they are flogged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that חזקיה must be the one who says 'they are flogged.' The proof is that חזקיה also says these witnesses are not executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: Conclude that חזקיה is the one who said they are flogged, since חזקיה said they are not executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out which side of the מחלוקת belongs to whom. It identifies חזקיה as the one who holds the kidnapping witnesses are flogged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions in the dispute were not labeled with names, so the גמרא works it out from another ruling. Since חזקיה holds they are not executed, lashes can still apply under his view. The next step explains why this cannot work for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And we said: Conclude
that it is Chizkiyya who said they are flogged,
from the fact that Chizkiyya said: they are not executed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמרינן: תסתיים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assigns the opinions in the dispute from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That חזקיה holds the false kidnapping witnesses are flogged
steps.raayaSupportSource: חזקיה's own ruling that kidnapping witnesses are not executed

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן cannot hold they are flogged
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the kidnapping witnesses are executed. That makes the prohibition a לאו whose warning leads to a court death penalty, and such a לאו never carries lashes. If the kidnapper himself is not lashed, the witnesses cannot be lashed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were רבי יוחנן: since he says they are executed, this is a prohibition given as a warning for a court death penalty. And for any such prohibition, one is not flogged. If he (the kidnapper) is not flogged, how could they (the witnesses) be flogged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its proof. רבי יוחנן's view rules out lashes, so the opinion that says 'they are flogged' must be חזקיה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין never carries מלקות. Under רבי יוחנן, the kidnapping prohibition is that kind of לאו, so the kidnapper is never lashed. עדים זוממין only get what the accused would have gotten, so they cannot be lashed either. That leaves חזקיה holding there are lashes, which brings back רב פפא's challenge in full force.

keyTerms.term: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition that serves as the warning for a court-imposed death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the witnesses could get a harsher or different punishment than the accused. עדים זוממין only get what they tried to bring on him, so if he would not be lashed, they cannot be lashed.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה holds that a kidnapper who has not sold gets lashes, so the defense in step 3 fails. רב פפא's question is now at full strength, and step 7 answers it by explaining the מחלוקת in a new way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear use of the rule that a לאו carrying a court death penalty has no מלקות. It shows how that rule shapes the punishment of עדים זוממין.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי יוחנן were the one who said 'they are flogged.'

phrases.english: since he says they are executed,
it is a prohibition
that is given as a warning for a court-imposed death penalty,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: and any prohibition that is given as a warning for a court-imposed death penalty,
one is not flogged for it.
He is not flogged,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the kidnapper, the one the witnesses testified against.

phrases.english: so how could they be flogged?

steps.triggerLanguage: דאי רבי יוחנן, כיון דאמר נהרגין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof in step 5, which completes the rejection of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the opinion 'they are flogged' cannot belong to רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת בית דין carries no lashes, combined with the rule that עדים זוממין receive only what the accused would have received

steps.title: A new explanation: the argument is only about the kidnapping witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the מחלוקת in a new way. Everyone agrees that עדים זוממין of the sale are executed. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן only argue about עדים זוממין of the kidnapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that the false witnesses to the sale are executed. The argument is about the witnesses to the kidnapping. חזקיה says they are not executed, because kidnapping is one act and selling is a separate act. רבי יוחנן says they are executed, because kidnapping is the beginning of the sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier way of explaining the argument fell apart, so רב פפא offers a brand-new way to understand what חזקיה and רבי יוחנן are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sale witnesses finish the whole case, so everyone agrees they get the death penalty if proven false. Kidnapping witnesses only describe the first part. חזקיה sees kidnapping as a separate act, so these witnesses cannot be killed for it. רבי יוחנן sees kidnapping as step one of the sale, so their testimony is part of a death case.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who testify that the kidnapper sold the person
Witnesses who testify that he kidnapped the person
It stands on its own, as a separate act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier steps. The word אֶלָּא means the old explanation is dropped. Under this new one, there is no argument at all about the sale witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the working explanation of the מחלוקת. It also sets up the question of how רבי יוחנן's idea works in other cases, like בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Regarding the witnesses of the sale,
everyone agrees that they are executed;
where they disagree is about the witnesses of the kidnapping.
Chizkiya says: they are not executed,
because kidnapping stands by itself
and selling stands by itself.
Rabbi Yochanan says: they are executed,
because kidnapping is the beginning of the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of the מחלוקת that steps 2-6 showed to be unworkable.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about the sale witnesses: חזקיה said they are not executed and רבי יוחנן said they are. That reading led to רב פפא's challenge and the lashes problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sale witnesses are executed according to everyone. The argument is only whether kidnapping counts as a separate act or as the start of the sale.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees about the first witnesses of a rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יוחנן admits that if the first witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה are proven false, they are not executed. They can say they only came to get him lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן agrees that the first witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה who were proven false are not executed. This is because they can say: "We came to have him lashed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a limit to רבי יוחנן's idea that 'the first part is the beginning of the death case.' It does not apply to the first witnesses of a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן סורר ומורה is first lashed, and only later, after he does it again, can he be put to death. So the first witnesses can honestly claim their goal was lashes, not death. That separates their testimony from any later death penalty, unlike kidnapping witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: The rebellious son described in the Torah
They were proven to be עדים זוממין (false witnesses)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan agrees
regarding the first witnesses
of a rebellious son, who were proven false,
that they are not executed,
since they are able to say:
"We came to have him lashed."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's view from step 7 by showing a case where he agrees the witnesses are not executed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first witnesses of a בן סורר ומורה who are proven false are not executed, even according to רבי יוחנן, because they can claim they came only for lashes.

steps.title: אביי's three-part summary of the rebellious son cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי lays out a summary. In two cases of בן סורר ומורה everyone agrees, and in one case there is a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: All agree in one case of a בן סורר ומורה, and all agree in another case of a בן סורר ומורה, and there is a disagreement in a third case of a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets up a three-part outline: two cases where everyone agrees and one case where they argue. The גמרא will now explain each part, one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line by itself does not tell us which cases are meant. It is a framework, and the explanations come in the next lines.
steps.confusionAlert: The three phrases sound almost the same. Each one refers to a different situation, which the גמרא is about to explain.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
All agree regarding a rebellious son,
and all agree regarding a rebellious son,
and there is a dispute regarding a rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's point about בן סורר ומורה and organizes all its cases into a summary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three situations of בן סורר ומורה witnesses: two agreed upon and one disputed.

steps.title: First case: everyone agrees the first witnesses are not executed
steps.stepSummary: The first agreed case is the first witnesses. If they are proven false they are not executed, since they can say they came only to have him lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees about a בן סורר ומורה regarding the first witnesses: they are not executed, since they can say "We came to have him lashed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first part of אביי's outline. It is the case of the first witnesses, which we just saw in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats step 8's ruling, now placed inside אביי's framework as the first 'everyone agrees' case. Since even רבי יוחנן agrees, it counts as a case where all agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Since they are able to claim

phrases.english: All agree regarding a rebellious son:
regarding the first witnesses, that they are not executed,
since they are able to say: "We came to have him lashed."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה: בְּעֵדִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item in אביי's three-part summary from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, including רבי יוחנן, agrees that the first witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה are not executed if proven false.

steps.title: Second agreed case: the last witnesses are executed
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that if the last witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה are proven to be עדים זוממין, they are executed. The first witnesses can say they only came to have him lashed, so the last witnesses are responsible for the whole matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees about a בן סורר ומורה that the last witnesses are executed. The first witnesses can say, 'We only came to have him lashed,' so these last witnesses did the entire thing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's summary and gives the second case where everyone agrees: the last witnesses are executed if they are proven false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first witnesses only led to lashes, so they are not seen as part of the death sentence. That means the last witnesses alone brought about the execution. Their testimony counts as a full matter (כולי דבר), not half a matter, so even חזקיה agrees they are executed.

keyTerms.meaning: The last witnesses, who testify after the son was already lashed
The first witnesses, whose testimony led only to lashes
We came to have him lashed
The entire matter, meaning full testimony and not half

steps.whatToRemember: The first witnesses are not executed because their testimony only led to lashes. The last witnesses are executed because they did the whole thing.

phrases.english: And all agree regarding a stubborn and rebellious son:
about the last witnesses, that they are executed,
phrases.notes: He means: if they are proven to be עדים זוממין.

phrases.english: since the first witnesses can say:
'We came to have him lashed,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי כּוּלֵּיהּ דָּבָר קָא עָבְדִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and these did the entire matter to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two agreed cases from אביי's summary
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה are executed if proven false, since they alone caused the execution.

steps.title: The disputed case: one pair saw him steal, another saw him eat
steps.stepSummary: The case that is disputed is when two witnesses say he stole in front of them and two others say he ate in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The dispute about a בן סורר ומורה is when two say, 'He stole in front of us,' and two say, 'He ate in front of us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's summary by giving the one case where there is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no single pair saw the whole crime. One pair saw only the stealing and the other saw only the eating. So the question is whether each pair is testifying to a full matter or only half a matter, which is the same kind of question as the kidnapping witnesses in the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole in front of us
He ate in front of us

steps.whatToRemember: Two cases are agreed on: the first witnesses are not executed, and the last witnesses are. The case where the testimony is split between stealing and eating is disputed.

phrases.english: And the dispute regarding a stubborn and rebellious son:
two say, 'He stole in our presence,'
and two say, 'He ate in our presence.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַחְלוֹקֶת בְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's summary with the disputed case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one pair testifies to the stealing and another to the eating, there is a dispute over whether they are executed.

steps.title: רב אסי: witnesses to the sale are not executed
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that witnesses who testify about the sale of a person and are proven false are not executed, because the accused could say he sold his own slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: Witnesses to the sale of a person who were proven to be עדים זוממין are not executed, since the accused can say, 'I sold my slave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב אסי about the kidnapping case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who saw only the sale did not prove a capital crime. Selling a person might be the legal sale of one's own slave. Since their testimony could not have gotten him killed on its own, they are not executed when proven false.

keyTerms.meaning: Who were proven to be עדים זוממין

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
Witnesses to the sale of a person who were proven false
are not executed,
since he can say, 'I sold my slave.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the kidnapping case with a new ruling about the sale witnesses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין of the sale in kidnapping are not executed, because the accused could claim he sold his own slave.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב אסי follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whose view רב אסי follows and answers that it is רבי עקיבא, who says witnesses must testify to a full matter and not half a matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view does רב אסי's teaching follow? רבי עקיבא's, who says testimony must be about a full matter, not half a matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to identify which תנא רב אסי's ruling is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף sees the sale witnesses as giving only half of the kidnapping story. רבי עקיבא holds that half a matter does not count as testimony. So he concludes that רב אסי must follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a matter, meaning testimony about only part of the crime

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַב אַסִּי?
phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this teaching of Rav Asi?
In accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says:
'A matter,' and not half a matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which תנא רב אסי's ruling depends on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי's ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who does not accept testimony to half a matter.

steps.title: אביי: רב אסי's reason works even for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects to רב יוסף. Would the witnesses be executed according to the רבנן? רב אסי's reason is 'since he can say I sold my slave,' and that reason applies to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does that mean that according to the רבנן they are executed? But רב אסי gave the reason 'since'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's claim that רב אסי's ruling depends only on רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי did not say 'because it is half a matter.' He said 'since he can say I sold my slave.' That reason does not depend on the rule of half a matter, so even the רבנן would agree the witnesses are not executed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who disagree with רבי עקיבא
But he said! A way of pointing back to the speaker's exact words

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. רב יוסף thinks the reason is 'half a matter.' אביי points out that רב אסי's actual reason is the claim 'I sold my slave,' which works according to everyone.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is it that if according to the Rabbis, they are executed?
But he said 'since'!
phrases.notes: אביי points to the word מתוך in רב אסי's ruling: 'since he can say I sold my slave.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דְּאִי כְּרַבָּנַן, נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רב אסי follows only רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אסי's stated reason ('since he can say I sold my slave') does not depend on the rule of half a matter, so it would apply even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree, when the kidnapping witnesses did not come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer to אביי. רב אסי's ruling can follow even the רבנן, because it is talking about a case where only the sale witnesses testified, and no witnesses to the kidnapping came.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can even say this follows the רבנן. It is a case where the witnesses to the kidnapping did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts אביי's objection and gives a new way to understand רב אסי. His ruling works for everyone, as long as only witnesses to the sale testified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי showed that the reason 'he can say I sold my own slave' fits every opinion, so tying it to רבי עקיבא made no sense. Now the case is narrowed: nobody testified that he kidnapped a free person. So the accused could never have been killed, and the false witnesses are not killed either.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the גמרא drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
You can even say it follows the רבנן

phrases.english: Rather, you can even say it follows the רבנן,
and it is where the witnesses to the kidnapping did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection by replacing רב יוסף's explanation with a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי follows only רבי עקיבא's rule of 'half a matter'
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אסי fits everyone. He is talking about a case where only the sale witnesses testified.

steps.title: Then why say something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אסי needed to teach this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If nobody testified about a kidnapping, of course the sale witnesses are not killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no kidnapping witnesses, the accused could never be killed in the first place. So false witnesses who only spoke about the sale could not be killed either. Why would רב אסי bother to say this?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new case-setup as making רב אסי's ruling obvious
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there were no kidnapping witnesses, there was never a death sentence, so the ruling teaches nothing new

steps.title: Even if the kidnapping witnesses came later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling teaches something new. The sale witnesses are not killed even if the kidnapping witnesses came afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the kidnapping witnesses did come in the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case more fully. The kidnapping witnesses did come, but only after the sale witnesses had already testified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once both testimonies are in, the sale witnesses become part of a death sentence. רב אסי teaches that this is not so. When the sale witnesses spoke, their words alone could not get anyone killed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where, even though they came in the end, they are still not killed.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the kidnapping witnesses, who came after the sale witnesses had finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲתוֹ לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by adding that the kidnapping witnesses came later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the kidnapping witnesses arrive, the sale witnesses are part of the death sentence
steps.terutzMaskana: The sale witnesses are judged by what their own testimony could do when they gave it

steps.title: Still, why say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: even with the later kidnapping witnesses, the ruling still seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. When the sale witnesses testified, they could not cause a death, so this is still obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are judged by what they tried to do when they testified. When the sale witnesses spoke, the kidnapping witnesses were not there yet, so the sale witnesses could not cause a death. The challenge is that even this version teaches nothing new.

phrases.english: But still, what is the point of saying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the 'obvious' challenge against the improved case
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the kidnapping witnesses came later (step 18)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the sale witnesses spoke, they could not cause a death, so it is still obvious they are not killed

steps.title: Hinting to each other counts for nothing
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the two pairs of witnesses hinted to each other. You might think hinting makes them one testimony, so רב אסי teaches that hinting means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where they were hinting to each other. You might have said that a hint counts for something. So it teaches us that a hint is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. Even when the sale witnesses and the kidnapping witnesses signal to each other, the sale witnesses are not killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hints make it look like the sale witnesses knew the kidnapping witnesses would come. That would make the two pairs look like one plan to get the man killed. רב אסי teaches that hints have no legal weight, so each pair is still judged only by its own testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: They are hinting to each other with signals
A hint is nothing (it has no legal weight)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי's ruling fits everyone, even the רבנן. Witnesses who only testified about the sale are not killed, even if kidnapping witnesses came later, and even if the two pairs hinted to each other, because hints count for nothing.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where they were hinting to each other.
phrases.notes: The two pairs of witnesses are signaling, as if they planned it together.

phrases.english: You might have said: a hint counts for something.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: רְמִיזָא לָאו כְּלוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: So it teaches us: a hint is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּקָא מְרַמְּזִי רַמּוֹזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second 'obvious' challenge by adding the hinting case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a case with a new point to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hinting turns the two pairs of witnesses into one testimony
steps.terutzMaskana: Hinting has no legal weight, so the sale witnesses are not killed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hints between witnesses do not join separate testimonies into one

steps.title: The משנה of the rebellious elder and the three courts
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a זקן ממרא, a sage who rebels against the court's ruling, is one of the people executed by חנק. The source is a פסוק in דברים. It also lists three courts that sat in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A זקן ממרא against the ruling of the court, as it says: 'If a matter is too hard for you in judgment.' There were three courts there: one sat at the entrance to the הר הבית, one sat at the entrance to the עזרה, and one sat in the לשכת הגזית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: the elder who goes against the court's ruling. The משנה gives the פסוק it is based on and describes the three courts that a dispute can go up to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקן ממרא is added to the list of people executed by חנק. The 'against the court' part is learned from the section in דברים that tells us to go up to the court and follow its ruling. The three courts are listed in order, from the outer gate to the highest court in the לשכת הגזית.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder: a sage who goes against the ruling of the court
Against the ruling of the court
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the great סנהדרין sat

steps.confusionAlert: The זקן ממרא is not punished just for having a different opinion. The משנה is setting up a process, and what counts as rebellion is explained later.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ זָקֵן מַמְרֵא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: משנה: A rebellious elder against the ruling of the court
phrases.notes: This משנה is part of the list of people executed by חנק, so 'is strangled' is understood.

phrases.english: as it says: 'If a matter is too hard for you in judgment.'
There were three courts there:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד יוֹשֵׁב עַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: one sat at the entrance to the Temple Mount,
and one sat at the entrance to the Temple courtyard,
and one sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ זָקֵן מַמְרֵא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקן ממרא who goes against the court is executed by חנק, based on דברים 17. There were three courts in ירושלים.

steps.title: Bringing the dispute to the first court
steps.stepSummary: The dispute first goes to the court at the entrance to the הר הבית. The elder lays out his view and his colleagues' view. If that court has a tradition on the question, it tells them the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They come to the court at the entrance to the הר הבית. He says: 'This is how I expounded, and this is how my colleagues expounded. This is how I taught, and this is how my colleagues taught.' If they have heard a ruling, they tell them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts describing the step-by-step process. The dispute goes to the first, lowest court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elder presents both sides, his own and his colleagues', both from a פסוק (דרשה) and from what they taught. The court answers only if it has a received tradition (אם שמעו). This sets up what happens when they have not heard one.

keyTerms.meaning: I expounded (learned a law from a פסוק)
If they heard (have a received tradition)

phrases.aramaic: בָּאִין לָזֶה שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: They come to the one at the entrance to the Temple Mount,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי, וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵירַי.
phrases.english: and he says: This is how I expounded, and this is how my colleagues expounded.
This is how I taught, and this is how my colleagues taught.
If they have heard a ruling, they tell them.
phrases.notes: 'They' first means the judges of this court, and 'them' means the elder and his colleagues.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאִין לָזֶה שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by describing the first stage of the process
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is first brought to the court at the entrance to the הר הבית. If that court has a tradition, it rules.

steps.title: The second court: at the entrance to the Temple courtyard
steps.stepSummary: If the first court has no tradition, the elder and his colleagues go to the court at the entrance to the עזרה. He presents both views again, and if they have a tradition, they tell them the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, they come to the judges at the entrance to the Temple courtyard. The elder says: This is how I explained it and this is how my colleagues explained it; this is what I taught and this is what my colleagues taught. If they heard a ruling, they tell them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the order of courts. When the first court has no answer, the dispute moves up to the second court, at the entrance to the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The process repeats exactly as in Step 22. Only the location changes, and this court is closer to the Temple. The court answers only if it has a tradition it "heard". It does not decide the question on its own reasoning here.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance to the Temple courtyard, where the second court sat
I explained (a law from the פסוקים)
My colleagues (the other sages in the dispute)
They heard, meaning they have a received tradition

phrases.english: And if not, they come
to those (judges) who are at the entrance to the Temple courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵירַי,
phrases.english: and he says: This is how I explained, and this is how my colleagues explained,
this is what I taught, and this is what my colleagues taught.
If they heard (a ruling), they tell them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו, בָּאִין לָהֶן לְאוֹתָן שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח עֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of courts from Step 22 and moves up to the second court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first court has no tradition, the dispute goes to the court at the entrance to the עזרה, which answers if it has a tradition.

steps.title: The final court: the Great Court in the Chamber of Hewn Stone
steps.stepSummary: If the second court also has no tradition, both sides go to the בית דין הגדול in the לשכת הגזית. Torah goes out from there to all of Israel, as the פסוק says, "from that place which ה׳ will choose".
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, both these and those come to the Great Court in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from which Torah goes out to all Israel, as it says: "From that place which ה׳ will choose."
steps.whatsHappening: The dispute reaches the top court, the בית דין הגדול. Its ruling is final for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower courts only passed on traditions they had heard. This court is the source of Torah for all of Israel, so it settles the question even without a tradition. The פסוק "from that place" shows that the binding ruling comes from the place ה׳ chose.

keyTerms.meaning: The Great Court, the סנהדרין of 71 judges
The Chamber of Hewn Stone in the Temple, where the Great Court sat
These and those: the elder and his colleagues (and the judges) together
Torah goes out, meaning binding rulings come from there

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole law of זקן ממרא. An elder can only be called a rebel once he goes against this final court, not the lower ones.

phrases.english: And if not, these and those come
to the Great Court that is in the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
from which Torah goes out to all of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "From that place which ה׳ will choose."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ בָּאִין לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next and final level after the court at the entrance to the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is finally brought to the בית דין הגדול in the לשכת הגזית, whose ruling binds all Israel.

steps.title: Teaching is exempt, ruling for action makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: The Great Court has ruled against him, and the elder goes home. If he only keeps teaching his old view, he is exempt. If he tells people to act on it, he is liable to death. The source is "and the man who acts with willfulness".
steps.simpleTranslation: He returned to his city and kept learning and teaching the way he used to: exempt. But if he ruled for people to act: liable, as it says, "And the man who acts with willfulness." He is not liable until he rules for action.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now states exactly what makes the elder a זקן ממרא. Teaching alone does not count. Telling people to act on his view does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is drawn between talking about the law and making it practical. The פסוק uses the word "יעשה", "acts", so liability needs a ruling that leads to action. Simply holding a different opinion is not rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled that people should act (a practical ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: The elder is not punished for disagreeing or even for teaching his opinion. He is liable only when he tells people to actually do it against the Great Court's ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: A זקן ממרא is liable only for a practical ruling (הוראה למעשה) against the בית דין הגדול. Teaching his view is not enough.

phrases.english: He returned to his city,
and he learned and taught in the way
that he used to learn: he is exempt,
but if he ruled that people should act: he is liable,
as it is said: "And the man who acts with willfulness."
He is not liable until he rules that people should act.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר לְעִירוֹ, שָׁנָה וְלִמֵּד בַּדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the Great Court rules, the משנה defines when the elder's continued disagreement makes him liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An elder who teaches against the Great Court is exempt. He is liable only if he rules for practical action.

steps.title: A student who rules is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד who has not been ordained and rules for action against the court is exempt. His stringency turns out to be his leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: A student who ruled that people should act is exempt. It turns out that his stringency is his leniency.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a final case: a student who is not yet an ordained elder. Even if he gives a practical ruling against the court, he is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student has a stricter rule: he is not allowed to issue rulings at all. Because of that, his ruling has no legal weight, so it cannot make him a זקן ממרא. The very restriction on him is what saves him from punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: A student, someone not yet ordained as an elder

steps.whatToRemember: Only an ordained elder can be a זקן ממרא. A student's ruling does not count, so he is exempt.

phrases.english: A student who ruled that people should act is exempt.
It turns out that his stringency is his leniency.
phrases.notes: His strict rule, that he may not issue rulings, is the very thing that gets him off.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהוֹרָה לַעֲשׂוֹת – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the liability rule of Step 25: it applies to an elder, not a student.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who rules for action against the court is exempt, because his lack of authority means his ruling does not count.

steps.title: The גמרא begins: a ברייתא on "If a matter is too hard for you"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that begins to explain the source פסוק of זקן ממרא, "כי יפלא ממך דבר".
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: "If a matter is too hard for you"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting a ברייתא on the פסוק behind the משנה. This line only opens the quote and sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא will go through the words of דברים 17:8 one at a time. It starts with "כי יפלא ממך דבר", which describes a question too hard to decide. The details are still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: If (a matter) is too hard or hidden
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: גמרא: The Rabbis taught:
"If a matter is too hard for you"

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כִּי יִפָּלֵא מִמְּךָ דָבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is finished. The גמרא now opens a ברייתא on the source פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a ברייתא that reads the פסוק "כי יפלא ממך דבר" word by word.
